note.text: Paraphrasing restates a source’s meaning using a different structure and wording. It is not a sequence of unrelated synonyms, and it must retain who did what, the time, causation and any qualification. Technical terms may need to remain. A paraphrase of someone else’s idea still needs acknowledgement where the task requires it; changed wording does not turn the idea into your discovery.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to restate an idea with changed wording and structure while preserving scope. Builds on: summary fidelity and word functions. Leads to: accurate directed writing and vocabulary.

sections.heading: Understand the pattern

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original source: Some members could not attend because the meeting ended after the last available bus. Faithful paraphrase: The meeting’s late finish prevented certain members from attending, given the available bus service. Some must not become all, and a transport constraint must not become a claim that members lacked interest. This is an invented practice source, not an actual attendance report.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: First explain the idea without looking at the wording, then compare your version with the original. Check actor, quantity, time, reason and certainty. Keep a necessary term rather than choosing a near-synonym that changes the claim.

pick.q: Paraphrase faithfully: The trial may reduce queues.
pick.r: The trial could make queues shorter.
w: The trial certainly ended every queue
Queues caused the trial to fail
e: May does not establish certainty or universality.
The source does not state that causal reversal.
The existence of a trial is supplied.
pick.y: Retain possibility and the intended effect.

pick.q: Paraphrase faithfully: Only registered members may borrow the folders.
pick.r: Borrowing the folders is restricted to registered members.
w: Registered members must borrow every folder
e: Only restricts eligibility.
Permission does not create an obligation.
That reverses the permission.
pick.y: Preserve the eligibility restriction and permission.

pick.q: Paraphrase faithfully: Bih delayed the meeting because the room was unavailable.
pick.r: The room’s unavailability caused Bih to postpone the meeting.
w: The meeting made all rooms unavailable
Bih delayed it because she disliked the members
e: A delay is not permanent cancellation.
That reverses the stated cause.
The proposed motive is invented.
